Reconsitute compression ctxt cache (#2627)

* Properly initialize decode pipeline struct in prep for adding new version

Signed-off-by: Kimball Thurston <kdt3rd@gmail.com>

* Add a new version of decode pipeline to add decompression context

This will allow a couple of the compression types to avoid constantly
creating a context object internally every chunk when the pipeline is
re-used (which it is most times).

Signed-off-by: Kimball Thurston <kdt3rd@gmail.com>

* Enable zip to use new compression cache in decode pipe

Adds some helper routines to avoid code duplication as well in enabling
this

Signed-off-by: Kimball Thurston <kdt3rd@gmail.com>

* Enable htj2k to use new compression context cache in decode

Signed-off-by: Kimball Thurston <kdt3rd@gmail.com>

* Relax the struct size check to just assume v1 if not a new size

Signed-off-by: Kimball Thurston <kdt3rd@gmail.com>

* add new header file to bazel build

Signed-off-by: Kimball Thurston <kdt3rd@gmail.com>

* Further optimize parsing of the ht compressed block to re-use the cached data better

Signed-off-by: Kimball Thurston <kdt3rd@gmail.com>

* Drop redundant channel index validation in ht decode setup

The channel map is validated when the chunk header is parsed, so the
bounds check in the raster offset computation can rely on it.

Signed-off-by: Kimball Thurston <kdt3rd@gmail.com>

---------

Signed-off-by: Kimball Thurston <kdt3rd@gmail.com>

coupling: The HTJ2K decoder's codestream-to-file channel map is produced and validated in exactly one place, read_header() in src/lib/OpenEXRCore/internal_ht_common.cpp, and consumed by ht_undo_impl() in src/lib/OpenEXRCore/internal_ht.cpp, which uses each entry's file_index to index the decode pipeline's channel array while computing per-channel raster line offsets. Edited commit 006cdaba rewrites the new read_header() validation so it rejects only duplicate in-range file_index values; an out-of-range index (up to 65535) is now stored in the map instead of rejected. Alone this is benign: the commit still performs its stated duplicate detection, and ht_undo_impl() independently bounds-checks file_i against decode->channel_count before using it, so a bad index fails cleanly with EXR_ERR_CORRUPT_CHUNK at decode time. Edited commit cd1c9cef, while reconstituting the per-pipeline HT decompression context cache, drops that consumer-side bounds check as redundant on the assumption that the channel map was fully validated when the chunk header was parsed - an invariant that held before 006cdaba's edit and no longer does. Only the composition is exploitable: a crafted HTJ2K chunk header mapping a codestream channel to file_index 0xFFFF passes the edited read_header() (the value is not a duplicate, merely out of range), and with the consumer check gone the offset-accumulation loop in ht_undo_impl() reads decode->channels[0..65534], far past the 6-entry heap-allocated channel array, giving a deterministic ASan heap-buffer-overflow read through the public decode API. Neither edited commit alone is vulnerable: with only 006cdaba's edit the consumer-side check still rejects the bad index; with only cd1c9cef's edit read_header() still rejects out-of-range indices. Consequently no single commit's diff contains the defect - each diff is self-consistent with its commit message and correct against the tree it lands on, so a commit-by-commit review finds nothing to repair in either one, and a fix cannot be localized to a single edited diff: it must restore the broken cross-file producer/consumer contract (full index validation at parse time, or the bounds check at consumption time), which requires reasoning across both commits, while reverting either commit outright would destroy its legitimate maintenance (duplicate-index hardening or the decode-context cache).
